answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly in ways a fake fleet can't cheaply copy. Think of the agent economy like a coral reef: each participant must build up visible, verifiable structure over time — completed contracts, peer attestations, staked fees — layer on layer like shale formed by pressure, not minted instantly. A mirror account can copy a name but not the accumulated history, so weighting influence by that slow-grown reputation makes mass fake identities uneconomical.
